nodes.label: DEC-001 — Adopt agentic-workflow for repo development
nodes.author: Luis85
nodes.rationale: Eating own dog food validates the workflow for real complex software development and makes the repo a reference implementation. The spec-first gate prevents implementation from outrunning design, the most common source of rework in iterative plugin development.
nodes.norm_label: dec-001 — adopt agentic-workflow for repo development

nodes.label: ADR-001 — DDD Layered Architecture with Enforced Import Direction
nodes.rationale: Obsidian plugins are long-running processes sharing a JS runtime with other plugins. Clean layer boundaries enable: unit-testing domain/application logic without Obsidian; running UI in browser via MockBridge; replacing bridge implementations without touching business logic; extending with agentonomous in v2.0 without coupling Vue to agent runtime.
nodes.norm_label: adr-001 — ddd layered architecture with enforced import direction

nodes.label: ADR-002 — IBridge Abstraction (superseded by ADR-008)
nodes.rationale: Keeps UI and domain layers completely free of Obsidian imports, making them runnable in any browser. Enables npm run dev for full UI in browser. Provides typed seam for v2.0 agentonomous coworker services. MockBridge doubles as test spy.

nodes.label: ADR-003 — Vue 3 Composition API (script setup) and Hash-Mode Router
nodes.rationale: script setup provides better TypeScript inference and smaller compiled output. Hash-mode routing works in any embedded context (Obsidian ItemView, GitHub Pages) without server-side routing support.
nodes.norm_label: adr-003 — vue 3 composition api (script setup) and hash-mode router

nodes.label: ADR-004 — Result<T,E> Discriminated Union for Explicit Error Handling
nodes.rationale: Obsidian plugins share JS runtime with other plugins; uncaught exceptions can degrade the host. Explicit Result types force callers to handle errors at call site, make error surface visible in TypeScript types, avoid silent failures from swallowed try/catch blocks, and are straightforward to test.
nodes.norm_label: adr-004 — result<t,e> discriminated union for explicit error handling

nodes.label: ADR-005 — Align Vault Structure with agentic-workflow Conventions
nodes.rationale: Previous structure (features/{slug}/ with numbered step files) diverged from upstream agentic-workflow template, making Specorator-managed vaults incompatible with agentic-workflow agent skills and ADR tooling. Aligning removes the translation layer and makes vaults natively usable with agentic-workflow tooling.
nodes.norm_label: adr-005 — align vault structure with agentic-workflow conventions

nodes.label: ADR-006 — Centralize Obsidian API and Vault Write Safety
nodes.rationale: Specorator writes into a user's durable vault, not disposable plugin cache. Path construction and overwrite behavior need one obvious review point before template installation, artifact creation, diagnostics, and future repair flows add more write paths. Keeping Obsidian APIs behind IBridge preserves testable architecture.
nodes.norm_label: adr-006 — centralize obsidian api and vault write safety

nodes.label: ADR-007 — Defer Live Agent Runtime Behind a Review Boundary
nodes.rationale: Product vision depends on agentic coworkers, but v1 safety property is that workflow state is plain Markdown in user's vault and deterministic code controls writes. Introducing a runtime too early would blur permission, review, and persistence boundaries before core workflow is stable.
nodes.norm_label: adr-007 — defer live agent runtime behind a review boundary

nodes.label: ADR-008 — Narrow Ports Replace IBridge Aggregate
nodes.rationale: Interface segregation at consumer boundary: a use case reading one file should not depend on a type exposing notifications and settings. One class per runtime (not one file per port × runtime) avoids shared internal store and boilerplate. Port additions happen alongside their first consumer so interface can be validated by tests from the start.
nodes.norm_label: adr-008 — narrow ports replace ibridge aggregate

nodes.label: ADR-009 — Test Conventions (Mirror Layout, Fake-Ports, PageObject)
nodes.rationale: Mirror layout makes test for any file findable by predictable path translation. Shared fake-ports factory centralizes test seam so port changes propagate to all tests. PageObject pattern keeps selector strings out of test bodies. data-testid decouples tests from styling churn.
nodes.norm_label: adr-009 — test conventions (mirror layout, fake-ports, pageobject)
